About the Company
Genmab is an international biotechnology company focused on developing innovative antibody therapeutics for cancer and other serious diseases. With a strong foundation in science, data, and innovation, Genmab brings together multidisciplinary teams to develop next-generation medicines and improve patient outcomes.
The company promotes a collaborative, purposeful, and inclusive culture where employees are encouraged to contribute innovative ideas and make meaningful scientific and business impact.
About the Role
Genmab is seeking a Director, Real-World Data & Epidemiology (RWD & Epi) Analytics to lead the design, execution, and communication of observational studies using diverse real-world data sources.
This strategic leadership role combines expertise in real-world evidence, epidemiology, observational study design, statistical programming, data infrastructure, and AI-driven analytics. The position will generate evidence supporting clinical development, market access, and health-policy decisions while partnering closely with cross-functional stakeholders.
The role is based in Plainsboro, New Jersey, with flexibility to work away from the office for 20%–40% of the typical schedule, subject to business and manager approval.
Key Responsibilities
Lead observational and epidemiologic studies from feasibility assessment through final reporting.
Evaluate claims, EHR, registry, and patient-generated data sources for research applicability.
Develop study protocols, analysis plans, statistical methods, programming specifications, and quality-control processes.
Apply advanced statistical methods, including survival analysis, regression, IPTW, MAIC, and causal inference.
Support survival and economic modeling for health technology assessment activities.
Present study designs, interim findings, and final results to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Evaluate emerging data sources, including genomics, biomarkers, clinical notes, and social determinants of health.
Lead implementation and scaling of AI applications within RWD and epidemiology analytics.
Mentor RWD and epidemiology scientists and programmers.
Establish standardized processes and governance for study execution and documentation.
Partner with data and technology teams to improve analytics infrastructure, reproducibility, security, and compliance.
Contribute to CORE department strategy and represent the organization on key initiatives.

Benefits & Perks
Competitive salary range of $231,280–$346,920 for U.S.-based candidates.
401(k) plan with 100% matching on the first 6% of contributions.
Medical, dental, and vision coverage.
HDHP with HSA option.
Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance.
Paid vacation, sick leave, and holidays.
12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave.
Child and adult backup care resources.
Family support and financial wellness programs.
Tuition reimbursement.
Commuter benefits.
Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses.
Potential discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives, depending on role eligibility.

Basic Qualifications
Master's or PhD degree in Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Public Health, or a related discipline.
10+ years of experience in real-world evidence generation and epidemiology analytics.
Demonstrated expertise in observational study design and advanced statistical methods.
Strong experience evaluating and working with real-world data.
Hands-on programming experience using SAS, R, or Python with claims/EHR data.
Experience with AI/ML frameworks.
Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Ability to work effectively in cross-functional and fast-paced environments.

Preferred Qualifications
Oncology experience.
Strong commercial and clinical strategic perspective.
Experience with emerging real-world data modalities.
Demonstrated research accomplishments and peer-reviewed publications.
Experience developing scalable analytics infrastructure and governance processes.
Strong leadership, mentoring, and technical coaching capabilities.
Experience applying AI to real-world evidence and epidemiology workflows.
